description: Common Paper and Bukkit errors. One object per rule, with a fixture that must trigger it.

rules.title: Out of direct (off-heap) memory
rules.explain: Network buffers ran out of space. This is separate from the normal heap, so raising -Xmx does not help. A plugin that handles packets, or a flood of traffic, usually causes it.
fix: Restart the server, then update packet plugins such as ProtocolLib and anti-exploit plugins.
Add -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=1G (or larger) to the start command.
If it keeps coming back, find the plugin with a spark profile and look at who allocates buffers.

rules.title: Invalid name used by a plugin or datapack: {1}
rules.explain: Something used the name "{1}", but Minecraft names may only use lowercase letters, digits and _ - . / characters. Uppercase letters and spaces are the usual mistake.
fix: Rename the item, key, recipe or function to lowercase with no spaces.
If a plugin created it, update that plugin or report it to the author.
rules.fixture: [10:00:00 ERROR]: net.minecraft.ResourceLocationException: Non [a-z0-9/._-] character in path of location: minecraft:MyKey

rules.title: Plugin was initialised twice
rules.explain: A plugin tried to create a second copy of itself. Either two jars of the same plugin are installed, or the plugin has a bug where it builds its own main class.
fix: Look in the plugins folder for two jars of the same plugin and delete the older one.
If there is only one, update the plugin or report it to the author.

rules.title: A plugin jar was replaced while the server was running
rules.explain: The server tried to read a class from a jar that was swapped or deleted after startup. Plugins stop working in strange ways until the server restarts.
fix: Never swap or update plugin jars while the server is running, and do not use /reload.

rules.title: A plugin tried to schedule work after it was disabled
rules.match: IllegalPluginAccessException: Plugin attempted to register task while disabled
rules.explain: A plugin that had already been switched off tried to start a task. This is a follow-on error. The real problem is whatever disabled the plugin earlier in the log.
fix: Scroll up to find the first error from this plugin, usually "Error occurred while enabling" or a crash, and fix that.
rules.fixture: [10:00:00 ERROR]: org.bukkit.plugin.IllegalPluginAccessException: Plugin attempted to register task while disabled

rules.title: Plugin listens for an event that does not exist: {1}
rules.match: Unable to find handler list for event (\S+)
rules.explain: A plugin tried to listen to {1}, which this server does not provide. The plugin is for a different server software or version, or the event comes from a plugin that is not installed.
fix: Check the plugin supports your server software (Paper, Spigot, Purpur) and version.
If the event belongs to another plugin, install that plugin.
rules.fixture: [10:00:00 ERROR]: Unable to find handler list for event com.example.FooEvent. Static getHandlerList method required!

rules.title: World contains entities that no longer exist: {1}
rules.explain: Entities of type {1} were saved in the world but nothing provides them any more, usually because a plugin or mod was removed. They are skipped and disappear.
fix: No action needed. Reinstall the plugin or mod if you want those entities back.
rules.fixture: [10:00:00 WARN]: Skipping Entity with id minecraft:oldmob

rules.title: Blocks of type {1} could not be loaded
rules.match: Tried to load a block entity for block (\S+) but failed at location
rules.explain: The world has {1} blocks with saved data, but the block no longer behaves like that type. This follows a version change or a removed plugin and is harmless once the block is replaced.
fix: No action needed. If a chest or sign lost its contents, restore that area from a backup.
rules.fixture: [10:00:00 WARN]: Tried to load a block entity for block Block{minecraft:chest} but failed at location BlockEntityType

rules.title: World was saved by a newer Minecraft version
rules.match: saved with newer version of minecraft! (\d+) > (\d+)
rules.explain: The world data version is {1}, but this server only understands up to {2}. Minecraft worlds cannot be opened by an older version after they were upgraded.
fix: Run the server on the Minecraft version the world was last saved with, or newer.
Or restore a world backup made before the upgrade.
rules.fixture: [10:00:00 ERROR]: java.lang.RuntimeException: Server attempted to load chunk saved with newer version of minecraft! 3955 > 3837
